business_outcome: Cut the time it takes a first-season reservations hire to answer Major Marine's conditional policy and logistics questions correctly, from a season of learning to a first week, without adding any risk of a wrong answer reaching a guest. Measured three ways against a baseline taken in the last six weeks of the 2026 season and re-measured in the same calendar weeks of 2027, weeks one through six after the March cohort starts. One, median time to answer a policy or eligibility question. Two, the escalation rate, the share of those questions a first-season agent hands to a supervisor or a veteran. Three, the count of policy misquotes that reach a guest, tracked as goodwill refunds or corrections issued after an agent quoted the wrong clock, fee or vessel. Success is a measurable fall in all three with no fall in guest experience. Explicit non-outcome, this is not about answering more calls or replacing anyone on the desk.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Staffed 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., seven days, year round, roughly a 70 hour week that never closes even off season. Packages bookable by phone only. Shuttle added by phone. On at least one reservation page online booking closes 12 hours out and the page tells the guest to call. The desk is a revenue channel, not just support.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes. The single point where the most conditional rules get applied by a person in real time.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: Mixed. Most high-cost questions are enumerable rules a decision table answers deterministically. The long tail of phrasing is where retrieval earns its place.

opportunity_map.area: Refunds, change fees and cancellation exceptions
opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Three refund clocks by booking contents, 72 hours cruise-only, 7 days cruise-and-hotel, 21 days once motorcoach or train is added. 3 percent card fee retained. One free date change to 24 hours out, then $15 per person. No-shows completely non-refundable and not transferable.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes, the cleanest case in the business. Structured inputs, published rules, output is a date, a fee and a sentence.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: NO AI NEEDED. A decision table. Exhaustively testable, zero hallucination surface, highest cost of a wrong answer.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Packages bookable by phone only unless noted. All discounts direct-only, not valid through third parties. Full payment at booking. Company owns Harbor 360 Hotel, Seward Gateway Hotel and a Seward Hertz franchise, so package ingredients are all in house.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes in principle. A configurator could assemble and take payment outside business hours.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: Little or no AI. Conventional commerce software. Largest unknown, the booking engine vendor is unidentified and may never be guessed, so integration can't be scoped from public facts.

opportunity_map.area: Trade, wholesale and third party channel
opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Only verified fact is that discounts are not valid through third-party reservations or travel agencies. Nothing else survived the gate.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Unknown on this evidence.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: Undetermined. Almost entirely unevidenced, must not be built on without new research.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: All cruises depart from the Harbor 360 Hotel office. The rail arrival case is explicitly footnoted on their own check-in page and is HANDLED. Guests stay aboard the whole cruise.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Marginally. A well documented single-point boarding operation with an owned lobby, unusually simple for the category.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: No. Nothing here is broken and the study must not imply it is.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Shuttle added by phone with 24 hours notice, advance reservations required, not available for the 8:00 a.m. 6 Hour cruise. Complimentary terminal loop 7:00 to 9:45 a.m. every 15 minutes, a 165 minute window. Distances 0.6 and 0.8 miles. Two of their own pages give different parking prices.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes. Eligibility is a three-condition rule that currently consumes a phone call each time.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: No AI. Deterministic. The parking contradiction is a website defect and never a headline.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Cruises go out rain or shine, only cancelled for unsafe sea conditions. If a full-day Kenai Fjords tour is limited to Resurrection Bay, partial refunds are offered. The Coast Guard certified Captain has discretion.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Partly. Who is affected, which departures have room, and drafting a consistent notification is mechanical once the Captain has decided. The decision stays with the Captain.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: Workflow automation with AI confined to drafting the guest message. Event frequency unpublished, which caps what can honestly be claimed.

opportunity_map.area: Rail connection and the late train
opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: The on-time case is carved out in a footnote and works. If the train is late the company says it will do its best to transfer passengers to another date or the 12:30 pm 4 Hour Cruise. Manual and discretionary.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes, narrowly. Which sailings have room and what each booking is owed is computable. The judgement is not.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: No AI for the lookup. Possibly AI for the message. Small surface.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Seating assigned by staff before the cruise. Vessels up to 192 passengers. Special requests not guaranteed.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Possibly, constraint solving is a solved class.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: Not AI, optimisation. NO evidence the current manual process is painful, so it stays on the map and is not built on speculation.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Vegetarian guests on the 6, 7.5 and 8.5 Hour cruises can request in advance at time of reservation. The 4 Hour has no meal.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes. Whether a request is even possible depends on the product and on catching it at booking time.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: No AI. A rule plus a prompt in the booking flow, same answer layer as the refund clocks.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Accessibility differs vessel by vessel. Five named vessels accessible on the first deck inside the main cabin only, outside decks not, no vessel takes a motorized wheelchair. The correct answer depends on which vessel runs the departure.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes, and cost of error here is the highest in the business.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: No AI. A join between the vessel roster and the departure schedule, currently done in a person's head.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Eight published vessels, 36 to 192 passengers, capacities summing to 1,074. Rachel Marie is described in the FAQ as running the 12:30 pm 4 Hour departure yet is absent from the fleet page. Unresolved.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes. Every accessibility, seating and capacity answer depends on this map, and the Rachel Marie discrepancy shows it lives in more than one place and the copies disagree.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: No AI. One authoritative table every other answer reads from.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: About 60 seasonal employees in Seward, peak hiring January 15th to April 15th, across Customer Service and Sales Staff, deckhands, engineering, inventory and dock support, cooks and occasionally captains. Housing from $15 per night, $400 travel reimbursement on contract completion. 2026 season March 7th to October 11th.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes. The workforce that applies the conditional rule set is rebuilt inside a 90 day window every year, then the season starts.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: The one place the strongest independent evidence points directly. Novices gained 34 percent while experienced workers gained almost nothing, which describes an annually resetting workforce precisely.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Thirteen captains with tenures 4 to 26 years, a Port Captain at 17. Shoreside leaders at 22, 15, 11, 8 and 4 years. Deep stable expertise above a base that turns over every year.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes, in one direction. The knowledge exists and is excellent, it is simply not written anywhere a first week hire can reach it at 4:40 p.m. on a Sunday.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: Retrieval over their own material, with veterans as the source of truth rather than the users.

opportunity_map.area: The two hotels and the Hertz franchise
opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Major Marine states it owns Harbor 360 Hotel, and Seward Gateway Hotel states it owns and operates Major Marine Tours. The owner also holds a Seward Hertz franchise. Boarding happens from the Harbor 360 lobby.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes. Cruise plus room plus car is an in-house package requiring a phone call, and two hotel front desks answer some version of the same cruise questions.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: Package assembly is conventional software. The hotel desks answering cruise questions is the same answer-layer problem, one corpus serving three counters.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Guests stay aboard the whole cruise. Meals differ by product.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Little that is verified.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: No. Leave it alone.

opportunity_map.area: Shoulder season and the season-end ladder
opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: Products fall away on a ladder, 8.5 Hour ends September 7, 7.5 Hour September 13, 6 Hour September 21, 4 Hour runs to October 11. Three departure slots end August 23. Orca Quest runs May 18 to June 20 and is absent from the five-product all-cruises index.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes on two fronts, shoulder-season yield and catalogue integrity.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: No AI for the catalogue. Yield work is unevidenced here and stays on the map.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: The 4 Hour Spring Wildlife Cruise is already published for March 20 to May 16, 2027 at $109 adult. Next season is selling while this one runs.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes, and it sets the clock. Anything meant to change the 2027 season has to exist before the March cohort arrives.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: Timing constraint rather than a build.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: A live 2026 booking page still carries copy about a cruise being new in 2021 and unavailable in 2020. Two pages give different parking prices. A booking page warns to allow several seconds for the engine to load. Orca Quest missing from the product index.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Yes, cheaply. A scheduled consistency check would catch a stale year, a contradicting price and a missing product.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: Mostly no AI, a diff and a rule set. Ordinary housekeeping, NOT operating problems, and may never headline anything.

opportunity_map.area: Discoverability and how AI assistants recommend them
opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: A 61,459 call audit across 12 models found responding to reviews moved recommendation probability +0.1 pp, statistically equivalent to zero, while guest rating moved it about +32 pp, review volume +8.31 pp and price -30.03 pp.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: This is a STOP-DOING finding, not a build. Money spent on review-response tooling buys nothing in this channel.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: No build. Worth handing them for free because it saves them a purchase they are actively being sold.

opportunity_map.whats_happening_now: A Maintenance Director with 15 years, eight published vessels, Engineering among the seasonal roles hired each year.
opportunity_map.could_software_change_it: Unknown, nothing verified describes the current state.
opportunity_map.ai_or_not: Undetermined. Stays on the map, does not get proposed.

target_opportunity.job: A reservations desk that is rebuilt from novices every spring has to apply a large conditional rule set correctly, seventy hours a week, for a seven month season, with only a policy page and a veteran's memory to lean on.
target_opportunity.why: Tops the Ulwick math and is the only opportunity where all four of Torres's factors line up at once. Sizing recurs every year without end because c24 makes the reset structural rather than a bad year. Market position is unusually strong, they already own the knowledge and the corpus is their own published policy rather than something we invent. Strategy fit is exact for a locally owned family company competing in the same harbour against a NYSE-listed operator, where service is the differentiator that is actually theirs to defend. It also absorbs four other scored jobs whole, refund clocks, accessibility routing, shuttle eligibility and dietary windows, so picking it does not cost the runners up. TWO CAVEATS STAY ATTACHED. Nothing implies a guest ever complained. The absolute headcount on the desk is unpublished, so this is dense in value per person and modest in total hours.
target_opportunity.forces: Push is structural and dated, 60 seasonal staff arrive January 15th to April 15th, the season opens March 7th, and the rule set has three refund clocks, two fee rules, a per-vessel accessibility matrix, a per-product dietary window and a shuttle exclusion. Pull is the strongest citation in the file, 5,179 agents where novices gained 34 percent and experienced workers gained almost nothing, plus i6 where a named day-cruise operator found its bot had quietly become a staff training tool. Anxiety is real, a confidently wrong policy answer reaching a guest is worse than a slow correct one and a first week hire can't detect it. Habit is near zero for the target user, the rarest and most valuable condition here. Push plus pull beats anxiety plus habit ON ONE CONDITION, that the thing is staff-facing with a human between it and the guest, and that it shows its source on every answer. That condition is what makes the forces balance.

candidate_builds.name: A. The Desk Brain
candidate_builds.what_it_is: An internal, staff-facing answer engine over Major Marine's own policy corpus. An agent types a question in plain language and gets the answer, the verbatim source sentence, the page it came from, and an explicit escalate path when the corpus does not cover it. Runs on the desk, on a phone for dock and hotel staff, and logs every question and every miss.
candidate_builds.ai_role: Retrieval over a bounded corpus plus a single grounded generation call with mandatory citation. No agent, no autonomy, no multi-step chain, so the compounding-error math never applies.
candidate_builds.why_it_might_win: Matches the target opportunity directly and covers the long tail of phrasing no rule set can enumerate. Strongest evidence in the file behind it. The corpus is small, clean, public and already written, which removes the number two project killer. One corpus serves the desk, the dock and both hotel front desks.
candidate_builds.why_it_might_lose: Retrieval systems answer confidently and wrongly, the exact failure a first week hire can't catch. Spends real money on questions a decision table answers for nothing. Without an eval set from actual questions the acceptance bar is a guess, and no evals means no promise.

candidate_builds.name: B. The Policy Decision Table
candidate_builds.what_it_is: A deterministic answer tool with no model in it. Encode the enumerable rules as an actual decision table, refund clock by booking contents, the 3 percent retained fee, the free change then the $15 per person, the no-show rule, shuttle eligibility, dietary request window by product, and accessibility by vessel joined to the departure schedule. The agent answers four or five structured questions and gets the date, the fee, the eligibility and the verbatim published sentence to read to the guest.
candidate_builds.ai_role: NONE. This is the low-AI candidate and it is here because the facts point at it, not to be a strawman.
candidate_builds.why_it_might_win: Exhaustively testable, so the acceptance bar is 100 percent and provable rather than a threshold on an eval set. Zero hallucination surface on exactly the questions with the highest cost of error. Cheapest thing on the list. Forces the authoritative vessel-to-departure table into existence, which c21 shows they do not currently have.
candidate_builds.why_it_might_lose: Only answers what can be enumerated in advance. A first week hire's real questions are not all clean rule lookups, and the tool is silent on everything outside its table. On its own it is half the outcome.

candidate_builds.name: C. Self-serve Package Builder
candidate_builds.what_it_is: Take packages off the phone. A configurator that assembles cruise plus Harbor 360 or Seward Gateway plus ground transport, prices it, applies the direct-only discount, takes payment and writes the booking, outside the 8 to 6 window.
candidate_builds.ai_role: Little to none. Conventional commerce software.
candidate_builds.why_it_might_win: Highest revenue ceiling on the list. Attacks c1, c2 and c3 together using assets the company already owns outright.
candidate_builds.why_it_might_lose: Three disqualifiers at this stage. The booking engine vendor is unidentified and may never be guessed, so the integration can't be scoped from public facts. Package volume and value are unpublished. And phone-only may be a deliberate margin and upsell decision by a sales organisation with a named Director of Sales, in which case we would be proposing to remove a revenue mechanism while calling it a fix.

candidate_builds.name: D. Guest-facing Website Chatbot
candidate_builds.what_it_is: The Black Cat shape. A bot on the website and messaging channels answering guest questions 24-7, wired toward the booking flow.
candidate_builds.ai_role: Retrieval plus generation, guest-facing, no human in the loop at answer time.
candidate_builds.why_it_might_win: The only candidate with a named, measured comparable in the same category. Black Cat Cruises reports 10 staff hours saved per month, 60 percent of questions answered and 15 clickthroughs per month on roughly a 100 passenger vessel. Major Marine is larger. Also serves guests outside the 8 to 6 window, which nothing else does.
candidate_builds.why_it_might_lose: The measured effect is modest, 10 hours a month is a fraction of a single shift, and the vendor's $3,750 figure is labelled potential bookings by the vendor itself. i7 is the tell, the same vendor's homepage claims 95 percent where its own case study reports 60. Most importantly it puts hallucination risk on the guest side of a thirty year reputation before any eval set exists. The right second move and the wrong first one.

candidate_builds.name: E. Voice Agent on the Reservations Line
candidate_builds.what_it_is: An AI answering the phone, handling hours, availability, FAQ, booking and routing, with handoff to a person.
candidate_builds.ai_role: Speech recognition, dialogue and synthesis in a real-time loop.
candidate_builds.why_it_might_win: Aimed at the highest-traffic surface in the business. On paper the biggest reach number on the list.
candidate_builds.why_it_might_lose: It is here because this desk has a documented habit of reaching for it, and it is scored so the room can be seen rejecting it on evidence. Independently measured latency ran 1,296 to 1,740ms median and no platform achieved sub-800ms. Smooth is under about 800ms, so every platform measured lands where callers feel slow. Worse, callers skew toward trouble, a late train, a re-route, a cancellation inside a clock. A guest whose train just failed meeting a bot that pauses a second and a half per turn is the worst first contact this company could buy.

candidate_builds.name: F. Disruption Console
candidate_builds.what_it_is: When the Captain re-routes or the train runs late, one screen shows who is affected, which remaining departures have room, what each booking is owed under the published policy, and a drafted notification for a human to approve.
candidate_builds.ai_role: Deterministic workflow for lookups and entitlement math, with a model confined to drafting the guest message.
candidate_builds.why_it_might_win: Targets the highest-stress moments and protects consistency exactly when a great reputation is most exposed. Seven live departure slots on a verified day means there is genuinely somewhere to move people.
candidate_builds.why_it_might_lose: The denominator is unknown and may be small. c11 states cruises go out rain or shine and are only cancelled for unsafe sea conditions, and c10's trigger is narrower than it first reads. Building a console for an event whose frequency is unpublished is how a project ends with no measurable P&L impact.

rice_and_cod.how_reach_was_set: HONEST CAVEAT FIRST. Annual passenger volume, call volume and the reservations headcount are all unpublished, and the 1,074 fleet seat sum is arithmetic on published capacities that must never be read as passengers carried. So no reach figure is a real count. Each is a 1 to 10 proxy for how much of the operation the build touches. Establishing the real baseline is the first two weeks of work on whatever gets picked, not an afterthought.

rows.cost_of_delay: HIGH AND DATED. Peak seasonal hiring runs January 15th to April 15th and the season opens March 7th, so the cohort this helps arrives in a fixed window each spring. Miss March 2027 and the value is zero until March 2028.
HIGH, same March 2027 gate, with one extra clock. It needs an eval set of real questions, and real questions only exist while the season is running, so the collection window closes with the season.
MODERATE. The unscopeable integration outweighs it.
NONE. Delay is a benefit here. The measured latency figures move in our favour over time and nothing is lost by waiting.

provisional_pick.name: The Reservations Desk Answer Layer, deterministic core first, grounded retrieval earned second
provisional_pick.what_it_is: ONE build in TWO funded phases against one outcome, not two projects. Phase one is candidate B in full, the decision table over the enumerable rules, plus the authoritative vessel-to-departure table it forces into existence, plus a MISS LOG that records every question the table could not answer. Phase two is candidate A, grounded retrieval with mandatory citations over the rest of the corpus, and it is funded ONLY if the phase one miss log proves the long tail is real and ONLY after that log has been turned into the eval set. THE MISS LOG IS THE EVAL SET, which is the part that usually does not exist and is why most of these builds have no acceptance bar.
provisional_pick.why_over_others: RICE ranks B first and A second, and they are not rivals, they are two rungs of the same ladder against the same job. The scoping method says walk the ladder and earn each step up, so the honest sequence is to take the rung that is exhaustively testable and free of hallucination on the highest-cost-of-error questions, then buy the model rung with evidence rather than optimism. Against D, the measured comparable is 10 staff hours a month at a smaller operator, and the same vendor page that reports it claims 95 percent where its own customer measured 60. It is not dead, it is the natural Next once the corpus and evals exist, and the same corpus serves it, which is the real argument for building the internal one first. Against C, the ceiling is highest and the floor unknowable, and assuming phone-only packages are a defect rather than a deliberate sales decision would be the exact sharpening reflex the fact-checker named on this run. Against F, the triggers are verified and the denominator is not. Against E, independently measured latency with no platform under 800ms against a caller mix skewed toward trouble makes it the worst first contact available, and it scored lowest, which is where it belongs.

what_the_scores_missed: Every reach number is a proxy and none is a count. Passenger volume, call volume and the reservations headcount are all unpublished. The first two weeks of the engagement are MEASUREMENT, not build, and the study should say so rather than dressing a guess as a denominator.

RICE has no term for COST OF ERROR, and this opportunity is defined by it. Quoting the 72 hour clock to someone holding a 21 day transportation package is a real dollar loss either way. That absence is the main reason the deterministic rung wins even though the AI rung has the stronger citation.
RICE rewards B partly for being cheap, which flatters it. B alone does not touch the long tail. B without A is half the outcome, which is why the pick is sequenced rather than split.

i1 is the strongest citation available and it is NOT a perfect fit. It measured software customer-support agents on issues resolved per hour, and this desk sells and solves travel logistics. The mechanism transfers, the magnitude may not. Confidence was cut to 75 percent and the study must present 34 percent as what someone else measured on someone else's workers, NEVER as Major Marine's number.

The adoption risk is habit and no score captures it. Colby Lawrence at 22 years, Rodney Roemmich at 15, Kirsten McNeil at 11 and Tayja Wright at 8 will not use this and should not be asked to. i1 found minimal impact on experienced workers, so a rollout aimed at everyone would look like a failure while a rollout aimed at the March cohort would match the evidence exactly. The rollout plan is part of the design, not a delivery detail.
Cost of delay is a STEP FUNCTION here, not a slope. Value is either in the cohort's hands before mid-March or worth nothing until 2028. RICE has no way to express a cliff.

The i2 and i3 finding is not a build and may be the most immediately useful thing we can hand them. Giving it away free saves them a purchase they are being actively sold, and it belongs in the study as advice with no invoice attached.

TWO CITATION WARNINGS FOR EVERY DOWNSTREAM AGENT. The Google 4.9 from 2,555 reviews and the 2.4 percent figure bind our behaviour as a constraint but are listed UNCOVERED_BY_THE_GATE and may NOT be quoted as facts. The field-wide no-self-serve-cancellation observation is also uncovered, so no candidate rests on it and none may.

pays_off.reasoning: It pays off for the reason the conscience document asks for rather than in spite of it. The pain is documented entirely from the company's own published policies, so not one word depends on a guest ever having complained. The workforce reset that makes those rules expensive is their own published fact. The strongest independent citation in the file measures its largest effect on precisely that population and almost none on the veterans, which tells us who to aim at as clearly as it tells us the effect is real. The corpus is small, public, already written and owned, which removes the number two cause of AI project failure before the project starts. The honest first phase needs NO AI AT ALL, and saying that plainly is what earns the second phase. The window is dated and near, the build is small, and the acceptance bar is falsifiable. THE ONE THING IT IS NOT IS LARGE. Absolute hours saved are modest because the desk is small, so the honest business case is a ramp-time and error-rate case that recurs every spring for as long as they operate, and the ROI section must argue it that way instead of inflating a headcount nobody published.
